chapter: Trent's band: Arkansas, Dallas and the Adolphus
title: Respect from audiences and Bobby the drummer
summary: The band has few race problems at the hotel and is treated like gods; the drummer Bobby drinks but is overlooked.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: DID YOU HAVE ANY PROBLEMS, NO RACE KIND OF PROBLEMS?
YOU PROBABLY DIDN'T HAVE AS MUCH AS SOME BANDS WOULD HAVE.
PLUS, BY THE FACT THAT YOU HAD BEEN PLAYING IN A PLACE LIKE THE ADOLPHIS.
PEOPLE PROBABLY GAVE YOU A CERTAIN AMOUNT OF RESPECT.
Oh, they did. They looked up us almost as god.
MOST OF THE GUYS IN THE BAND, YOU DIDN'T HAVE ANY REAL BAD DRUNKS. I GUESS BOBBY WAS PROBABLY THE WORST.
Yeah, but he was such a fine gentleman and such fine drummer, he was OVERLOOKED.
Yeah. That band was the greatest thing I ever played in.
